# Herdr: Drain sessions before switching to cheap mode

> When the herdr extension chooses to switch the proxy to cheap mode due to
> inactivity, it first waits until the active session count falls to the number
> of slots available in cheap mode. No new work items are dispatched until this
> requirement is met and the proxy has been switched to cheap. If an interactive
> command is given while draining, the switch is cancelled and the time is reset.
> The inactive time is set to 15 minutes.

## Problem statement

When the herdr mode-switch worker detects operator inactivity, it switches the
llama-proxy from fast (3-slot cloud-backed pool) to cheap (2-slot local-first
pool) mode. Currently this switch happens immediately once the idle threshold
is met and the proxy reports idle. This can interrupt in-flight operator work
that happens to be using a slot at the moment of the switch, and it can allow
more active sessions than the cheap pool can sustain (up to 3 in fast mode,
only 2 in cheap).

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** -- wants the proxy
  to drop to cheap mode based on their absence, but only after active work has
  naturally subsided to fit within the cheap pool.

User story:

- *As an operator, when I stop issuing agent-route commands through the herdr
  plugin for the idle window, I want the proxy to drain active sessions down to
  the cheap pool size before switching -- so I do not lose in-flight work and
  the cheap pool has capacity. If I return (issue a command), I want the process
  to cancel and reset.*

## Original acceptance criteria (drain plan — withdrawn)

- [ ] **Drain state:** when the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports
  idle, the mode-switch worker enters a **draining** state instead of switching
  immediately. It periodically checks whether the active session count (busy
  slots) has fallen to <= the cheap mode slot budget (2, i.e.
  `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` free slots).
- [ ] **Dispatch pause during drain:** while in the draining state, the downtime
  dispatcher does **not** dispatch new work items. Existing in-flight work
  continues; the idle gate prevents new panes from spawning.
- [ ] **Drain completion:** once the proxy reports sufficient free slots (>= 2
  free), the drain ends and the proxy switches to cheap mode immediately.
- [ ] **Drain cancellation:** if an operator issues an agent-route command while
  draining, the drain is cancelled, the switch-to-cheap is abandoned, and the
  idle timer resets to "active now" (the proxy stays fast).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** skip when the persisted mode
  already matches the target; 409 treated as no-op; single-flight; at most one
  switch per state change.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, and ambiguous
  payloads yield no switch; the worker stays in its current mode.
- [ ] **Idle threshold changed:** the default `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` is
  changed from 60 minutes to 15 minutes.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit tests cover -- drain state entry/exit, dispatch pause,
  operator-command cancellation, threshold change, all existing fail-closed
  paths unchanged. Full project suite green.

## Constraints

- The cheap mode slot budget is 2 slots (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`). The
  drain condition is `freeSlots >= 2`.
- Draining must not kill in-flight work -- it only prevents *new* dispatches.
- The fast direction (operator command --> mode=fast) is unaffected; only the
  cheap idle switch path changes.
- The existing idle-clock reset mechanism (`lastOperatorCommandAt`) is reused
  for drain cancellation.
- Fail-closed remains the safe default at every boundary.

## Existing state

- The mode-switch worker (`mode-switch-worker.ts`) already tracks operator
  activity, polls `/llama/local/status` for idle evaluation, and switches to
  cheap on idle.
- The downtime worker (`downtime-worker.ts`) already controls dispatch based on
  the idle gate (`evaluateIdle`).
- The cheap mode slot budget is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` (parent
  WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR).
- The default idle threshold is `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000`
  (60 minutes).

## Desired change

Add a **draining** sub-state to the mode-switch worker's idle-to-cheap path:

1. **Entry:** After the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports idle, enter
   the drain state instead of switching.
2. **Polling during drain:** Each tick, check whether `freeSlots >= 2`. If so,
   switch to cheap and exit drain. If not, continue draining.
3. **Dispatch signal:** While in drain state, signal to the downtime worker to
   pause new dispatches.
4. **Cancellation:** If `onOperatorCommand()` fires during drain, exit drain
   immediately, reset the idle clock, and keep the proxy in fast mode.
5. **Default threshold:** Change `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` from
   3,600,000ms (60 min) to 900,000ms (15 min).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` -- Add draining state, drain logic,
  cancel on operator command, threshold constant change
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` -- Drain state tests, cancel
  tests, dispatch-signal tests
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` -- Respect drain signal from mode-switch
  worker to pause dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` -- No change (threshold constant lives in
  mode-switch-worker, settings re-reads it per tick)

## Related work

- **WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR** -- Per-slot operator gate for cheap switch (completed)
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** -- Activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9** -- Leader-only cheap switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU4MKVR4005WPBJ** -- Idle-trigger sources (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F** -- Tests: mode-switch worker core (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EEHQI002MOVT** -- Implement: mode-switch worker core (completed)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Adding a drain state introduces a new state machine transition path.
  **Mitigation:** Keep the drain logic simple -- poll free-slots each tick,
  cancel on command. Reuse existing single-flight and fail-closed mechanisms.
- **Risk:** Race between operator command and slot freeing during drain. If both
  happen simultaneously, the operator command path takes priority -- the drain
  cancels and the idle clock resets, so the proxy stays fast. This is the
  correct user-facing behaviour.
- **Assumption:** The downtime worker can receive a signal from the mode-switch
  worker about the drain state. This is implemented via a callback on the
  mode-switch worker or a shared holder method (index.ts already uses the
  `modeSwitchHolder` pattern for the worker reference).
- **Assumption:** The "number of slots available in cheap mode" is the constant
  `DOWTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`.
- **Assumption:** Process restart during drain is safe -- the idle clock already
  resets to "active now" on construction (fail-safe: proxy stays fast until a
  fresh full idle window passes).
- **Scope control:** Making the drain threshold configurable is a follow-up
  opportunity, not in scope for this work item.
- **Scope control:** No change to the fast-switch path (operator command -->
  mode=fast); only the cheap idle-switch path gains drain semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was completed without additional questions -- the work item
description provided sufficient detail to draft a clear brief.

## Revision (2026-10-06): verification, intent, and decision

### Verification outcome

All five children reached a terminal stage and their commits are on `dev`
(`956237e6`, `2c3db331`, `386733c1`, `a22442d0`, `d9ea2100`); unit tests
(66 in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts`) and the drain-dispatch integration tests
(3) are green. The feature is nevertheless **broken in production and has
never once completed a drain**.

### Root causes (why it can never work as written)

1. **Slot model inverted.** The brief assumed fast = 3 slots and cheap = 2.
   The live proxy config is the reverse: fast = 1 slot (`config.yaml`,
   `session_slot_pool_size: 1`), cheap = 3 slots (`config-cheap.yaml`,
   `session_slot_pool_size: 3`; raised 2 -> 3 after this brief was written).
   So cheap has *more* capacity than fast, and there is nothing to shed.
2. **Budget borrowed from the wrong constant.** Drain completion requires
   `freeSlots >= MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, which was set to
   `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`. That constant is the minimum free
   slots an *audit dispatch* needs (parent + Phase 2 child) -- not the cheap
   pool size. In a 1-slot fast pool `freeSlots` can never reach 2, and
   `isIdleStatus` returns false whenever `required > total_slots`, so
   `evaluateIdle(status, 2)` is permanently false.
   (`mode-switch-worker.ts:116,619`; `downtime-worker.ts:817-828`.)
3. **The drain is unbounded.** Unlike the server-side drain (capped at
   `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_MAX_SECONDS`), the client drain has no timeout -- only
   operator-command cancellation. Once entered it therefore latches:
   `getIsDraining()` stays true and the downtime dispatcher stops issuing new
   panes until an operator command arrives.

### Intent reconstruction -- the client drain is a *sibling* of the server-side drain

The proxy already carries a **bounded mode-switch drain**
(`LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE` / `LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H`). Both mechanisms have the same
shape: defer a mode transition, stop admitting **new** work during the
deferral, and let **in-flight** work finish without killing it.

| | Server-side (proxy) | Client-side (herdr plugin) |
|---|---|---|
| Armed by | `set_mode` (switch already requested) | idle window met + proxy idle |
| Defers | the proxy restart | the `POST /admin/set-mode cheap` |
| New work | chat requests get 503 + Retry-After | downtime dispatches paused (`drainPaused`) |
| Waits for | in-flight local streams | `freeSlots >= budget` |
| In-flight work | never killed | never killed |
| Bound | **bounded** (`MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_MAX_SECONDS`, 90s) | **unbounded** -- operator command only |

The dispatch pause is load-bearing specifically *because* the switch was made
**deferred** rather than immediate: the downtime dispatcher's job is to fill
idle proxy capacity with backlog work, so left alone it keeps re-occupying the
slots the mode-switch worker is trying to accumulate, starving the completion
condition. Pausing new dispatches is what lets the pool quiesce and the switch
proceed. (This starvation role is *not* stated in the original brief, which
framed the drain around in-flight protection and capacity fit; it is a
reconstruction consistent with the code and with the dispatch-pause comment in
`downtime-worker.ts`.)

The **starvation rationale remains conceptually valid**; the **capacity-fit
rationale is inverted** by the current config. The sibling relationship is
structural, but the client drain did not copy the server drain's most important
property: the time bound that stops a stream of new work from postponing the
transition forever.

### Evidence

- No `draining` decision entry exists in any retained
  `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (all 100 entries are `checkin`).
- Proxy log (2026-10-06, retained window 07:55-09:26): the only fast->cheap
  switch (09:19:13) was not reachable via the drain path -- the shared idle
  clock was last set at 09:06:41 (12.5 min < 15 min) and the completion gate is
  unsatisfiable anyway. Startup lines confirm `mode=cheap ... slots=3` and
  `mode=fast ... slots=1`.
- Live proxy at verification time: `GET /admin/mode` -> `fast`;
  `GET /llama/local/status` -> `total_slots=1`.

### Decision

**This feature is no longer needed and is withdrawn.** It is superseded by the
proxy's own schedule (`mode_schedule.yaml`: cheap 01:00-10:00, fast 10:00-01:00)
and the server-side bounded drain, both of which own transition mechanics
correctly. The blocking defect filed during verification is
**WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM** (superseded once the revert lands).

### Recommended remediation

See the `## Recommendation` section below.

## Recommendation

### Recommended end state

Reclaim a single coherent mode-transition story: **the proxy owns all
transition mechanics; the herdr plugin is a thin policy layer that only chooses
the target mode.** Concretely:

- Keep the plugin's two signals -- **fast on operator command**
  (`onOperatorCommand`) and **cheap on operator idleness** -- plus the existing
  safeguards (leader-only cheap switching, shared cross-pane activity, the
  server-side fast->cheap cooldown).
- Put **no** slot-budget or dispatch-pause logic in the plugin. Any need to
  quiesce before a restart is already met by the proxy's bounded server-side
  drain.
- Never hardcode pool sizes in the plugin: derive from the live proxy status or
  don't reference them at all. (The cheap pool silently changed 2 -> 3 after
  this brief; that drift is what made the hardcoded `2` unreachable.)

### Work to be done (recommended order)

1. **Revert the drain mechanism** (F1/F2/F4/F5 equivalents). Reuse this parent
   as the revert work item, or create a child:
   - `mode-switch-worker.ts`: remove `draining`, `getIsDraining()`,
     `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, the `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` import,
     and the drain-clearing branches; restore the direct
     `await fireSwitch(opts.proxyUrl, 'cheap')`.
   - `index.ts`: remove the single `drainPaused:` line.
   - `downtime-worker.ts`: remove `drainPaused?: boolean` from the config type
     and the `if (cfg.drainPaused === true)` gate.
   - Tests/docs: delete `drain-dispatch-integration.test.ts`; remove the
     drain-specific cases from `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` /
     `downtime-worker.test.ts`; drop the drain paragraphs from
     `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.
   - Prefer a targeted manual revert over `git revert` of the five SHAs:
     unrelated commits landed between them in the same files, so raw reverts
     will conflict, while every drain line is still cleanly attributable to the
     feature commits.
2. **Decide the idle threshold (F3/AC7).** The 15-minute default is separable
   from the drain. Recommended: **keep 15 minutes** (responsive cheap-on-idle)
   unless the observed mode-churn argues for the original 60; record the choice.
3. **Add a regression guard.** A test pinning that the mode-switch worker does
   **not** gate the cheap switch on a slot count (and does not import audit slot
   budgets), so the inverted-budget bug cannot silently return.
4. **Close the lifecycle loop.** Mark `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM` superseded/won't-fix
   once the revert merges; re-run `/skill:test` and `/skill:audit` on this
   parent; advance to release only after the revert is green.
5. **Only if starvation is later observed**: add a **bounded** dispatch pause
   modelled on the server-side drain (`max_seconds`, direction-aware), not a
   free-slot gate. Do not reintroduce an unbounded client drain.

### Non-goals / cautions

- Do **not** duplicate the server-side restart drain on the client. The proxy
  already defers new chat requests and waits (bounded) for in-flight streams.
- Do **not** remove the fast-on-command switch: the proxy schedule alone would
  leave the operator in cheap during 01:00-10:00 while actively working.
- Keep the drain and mode-switch concerns separate from dispatch scheduling;
  coupling them (as this feature did) lets a bad mode-switch condition stall
  work dispatch for the whole machine.

### Open decisions for the operator

1. Idle threshold after revert: **15 min (recommended)** or 60 min.
2. Idle cheap switch: **keep** (recommended) or delegate entirely to
   `mode_schedule.yaml`.
3. Whether to file a small, separate `docs`/`chore` item recording the
   fast/cheap slot-count contract so future client logic cannot assume a pool
   shape.

## Decisions (2026-10-06)

Operator confirmed:

1. **Idle threshold after revert:** keep **15 min** (`900_000` ms).
2. **Idle cheap switch:** **keep** -- the plugin retains the cheap-on-idle signal.
3. **Revert scope confirmed:** revert F1/F2/F4/F5 (drain state, dispatch-pause
   wiring, drain tests, drain docs); keep fast-on-command; leave the proxy's
   server-side bounded drain untouched; the client drain is removed entirely.
4. **Slot-count contract:** chore filed -- **WL-0MUWH45RF004URWP**.
5. **Stale `lastKnownMode` gap in the fast path:** **fix now**, in scope.
6. **Implementation item:** reuse this item as the epic -- the revert is a child, **WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR** (`Implement` cannot target an all-terminal parent directly: `phase_parent` advances it instead of working it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The client drain mechanism is removed from `mode-switch-worker.ts`
      (`draining`, `getIsDraining()`, `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, the
      `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` import, drain-clearing branches), and the
      cheap path calls `fireSwitch('cheap')` directly.
- [ ] `drainPaused` is removed from `index.ts` and `downtime-worker.ts`.
- [ ] Drain tests and `drain-dispatch-integration.test.ts` are removed; docs
      are trimmed.
- [ ] `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` remains `900_000` (15 min).
- [ ] Cheap-on-idle and fast-on-command are both retained, with the existing
      leader-only / shared-activity safeguards.
- [ ] The command-path fast switch is robust to a stale cached mode: an agent
      command issued while the proxy is actually cheap always results in a fast
      switch (no reliance on a possibly-stale `lastKnownMode`).
- [ ] Regression test: the mode-switch worker does not gate the cheap switch on
      a slot count and does not import audit slot budgets.
- [ ] Full project suite green; `/skill:test` then `/skill:audit` clean.

# Own-backlog dispatch fallback must relinquish leadership

discovered-from:WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9

## Problem statement

WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 restricted downtime dispatch to the operator's sprint-view
window: when nothing in the view is dispatchable the dispatcher no-ops. The
operator has explicitly accepted that starvation trade-off **for that item**
(a non-critical item outside the visible sprint may go undispatched).

This item adds a bounded escape valve with a fairness guard:

> If there are no work items available to the dispatcher (nothing dispatchable
> in the sprint view), it may choose work from **its own backlog**. Once it has
> dispatched something from its own backlog, it must **relinquish the leadership
> role** so another instance can take over leadership.

The intent is to let the fleet keep working when a single root's sprint view is
momentarily empty/blocked, without any one instance monopolising leadership by
continually reaching into its own hidden backlog.

## User stories

- *As an operator*, when my sprint view is empty or fully blocked, I want the
  leader to still be able to pick up work from its own backlog, so capacity is
  not wasted.
- *As an operator*, once the leader has used that privilege, I want it to hand
  leadership over, so dispatch is shared fairly across instances.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Own-backlog fallback when the view is empty.** When the sprint-view head
   yields no dispatchable candidate (the existing terminal reasons —
   `no-candidate`, `review-queue-hold`, `code-freeze`, `fresh-audit-skip`,
   `audit-in-flight`, `audit-host-saturated`, `in-flight-hold` — or a genuinely
   empty view), the leader MAY fall back to its **own worklog backlog** (items
   beyond the sprint-view window). Verification: unit tests assert that with an
   empty/fully-filtered in-view head and an eligible out-of-view item in the
   leader's own root, the item is dispatched.

2. **Fallback is scoped to the leader's OWN root.** The fallback never reads or
   dispatches another instance's or another worklog root's hidden backlog.
   Verification: tests assert the fallback head lookup is made against the
   leader's own `cwd`/root only.

3. **Canonical ranking preserved.** The fallback re-reads the SAME ranking path
   (`fetchNextItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`) with a bounded
   larger window; it is a window extension, never a second ranking. Verification:
   ordering assertions on the fallback candidate.

4. **Leadership is relinquished after an own-backlog dispatch.** On a successful
   dispatch sourced from the own backlog (not from a normal in-view candidate),
   the instance MUST voluntarily step down via the existing
   `LeaderElectionManager.releaseLeadership()` so another instance can win the
   next election. Verification: a test asserts `releaseLeadership()` is called
   exactly once after a successful own-backlog dispatch, and NOT called after a
   normal in-view dispatch.

5. **Step-down never undoes the dispatch.** The claim / dispatch marker / spawn
   for the own-backlog item are completed before (or atomically with) the
   hand-off; the step-down must not roll back a pending dispatch, and the
   dispatched pane is not orphaned. Verification: after the fallback dispatch the
   item is claimed/marked and a pane is spawned, while the next tick observes the
   instance as non-leader.

6. **No step-down when the fallback finds nothing.** If no eligible own-backlog
   item exists, leadership is retained and the existing terminal reason is
   reported unchanged. Verification: tests assert no `releaseLeadership()` call
   and the pre-existing reason.

7. **All existing safety gates still apply** to the own-backlog candidate as
   sequential filters: scheduled-prompt, code-freeze, producer-review,
   dispatched-marker, per-tier free-slot minimums, active-audit single-flight,
   audit-host saturation, freshness/recency, CAS claim, spawn. Verification: the
   existing gate tests continue to pass unmodified, plus one integration test
   that a gated out-of-view item is still filtered.

8. **Critical behaviour unchanged.** `critical` items remain mandatory in the
   view with the existing critical-first escalation; this fallback is only for
   the no-dispatchable-in-view case. Verification: existing critical-first tests
   pass unmodified.

9. **Bounded and fail-open.** The fallback window is bounded (reuse/extend
   `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` or a new named bound); a `{ok:false}` lookup, a
   thrown error, or an empty fallback head degrades to the original terminal
   reason and never panics. Verification: fail-open tests.

10. **Documentation updated** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the
    own-backlog fallback + leadership hand-off contract, and
    `packages/herdr/README.md` matches.

11. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **No second ranking.** Reuse the canonical Herdr ranking path with a larger
  window; safety gates remain filters, never a fallback ordering.
- **Reuse the existing election primitive.** Use
  `LeaderElectionManager.releaseLeadership()` (`leader-election.ts`); do not
  invent a new hand-off mechanism or persistence.
- **Own root only.** `browseItemCount` remains the view bound; the fallback
  deliberately reads beyond it, but only from the instance's own worklog root.
- **Fail-open preserved.** A fallback lookup failure must not convert a defined
  outcome into a new failure.
- **No new persistence mechanism** and no coordination-file schema change.
- **No regressions** to TUI rendering or the existing sprint-view-only contract.

## Assumptions (confirmed at intake)

- **A1:** The fallback targets the highest-ranked eligible item from the leader's
  own backlog (canonical ranking), not an arbitrary pick — "anything from its own
  backlog" means "not restricted to the sprint-view window", not "random".
- **A2:** "Relinquish leadership" is a voluntary step-down
  (`releaseLeadership()`), clearing the lease/lock so the next election is won by
  another instance; the instance may re-acquire on a later tick under the normal
  election rules.
- **A3:** The step-down happens once per successful own-backlog dispatch, in the
  same tick as the spawn, and does not trigger an immediate self re-election in
  that tick.

## Open questions (resolved at intake)

- **Q1 — legacy mode (resolved: A).** The fallback is **coordination/leader
  mode only**. Evidence: `leaderManager` is constructed only when
  `opts.coordinationDir` is set (`downtime-worker.ts` ~L5634) and is `null` in
  legacy mode, where `leaderState` is hard-coded `true` (~L5663). With no
  leader-manager/peers there is nothing to relinquish, so legacy keeps today's
  behaviour.
- **Q2 — step down with no eligible peer (resolved: unconditional step-down).**
  AC4/AC6 are authoritative and carry no peer-presence condition: a successful
  own-backlog dispatch always steps down; a fallback that finds nothing never
  does. `releaseLeadership()` only deletes the lock + lease files, so with no
  peer the same instance simply re-wins the normal election on the next tick
  (bounded by the existing election backoff) — no new peer-detection mechanism
  is required. The only external marker of peers is coordination entries, which
  are removed on dispatch, so a reliable "eligible peer" predicate does not
  exist; adding one is out of AC scope and against the simplicity constraint.
- **Q3 — rate limiting (resolved: none beyond the existing cooldown).** The
  fallback only fires when the view yields no dispatchable candidate, and at
  most one step-down occurs per fallback dispatch; the existing no-candidate
  cooldown plus election backoff already bound churn. Revisit if churn is
  observed.

## Risks

- **Leadership churn.** Frequent fallback dispatches could cause repeated
  elections and idle windows. *Mitigation:* fallback only fires when the view is
  empty, at most one step-down per fallback dispatch, subject to the existing
  election backoff; Q3 rate-limiting if needed.
- **Fairness vs. throughput.** Stepping down when no peer can take over would
  idle the machine. *Mitigation:* Q2 (retain when no eligible peer).
- **Root leakage.** A naive implementation could dispatch another root's hidden
  backlog. *Mitigation:* AC2 own-root-only tests.
- **Scope creep (window size / peer detection / rate limiting).** Tuning the
  fallback window, adding a peer-eligibility predicate, or introducing a
  fallback-specific rate limiter are tempting but outside the ACs.
  *Mitigation:* keep the window a reused/renamed existing bound; record any such
  opportunity as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — fallback read + dispatch in
  `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchFromCoordination` / the leader loop; wire the
  step-down after an own-backlog dispatch; possibly extend
  `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` usage.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — existing `releaseLeadership()`
  (reused, likely no change).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getHerdrListHead` / deps wiring if a
  separate fallback limit is needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.test.ts` — fallback + step-down tests.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — contract docs.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9** (completed/in_review) — sprint-view-only dispatch
  window; accepted the starvation trade-off this item relieves. Discovered-from
  source.
- **WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5** (completed) — original extended dispatch window
  (removed/restricted for non-critical work by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9). This item
  reintroduces a *bounded, own-root, leadership-handing-off* fallback rather than
  the previous unconditional extension.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — "dispatcher == Herdr list head; gates
  are filters" contract.
- **WL-0MTMPSCL8000O45H** — coordination check-in / leader lease cadence.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT5MJXI0004DKFX** – Fix effortOrdinal in database.ts — add word-boundary fallback (completed)
- **WL-0MUKXFW3N003RZSK** – Test: item-ID tab anchor and dispatch wiring (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Does the own-backlog fallback apply in legacy mode (no
  `coordinationDir`; the instance is always "leader" with no peers)?
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** No — coordination/leader mode only.
  `leaderManager` is created only when `coordinationDir` is set; legacy mode has
  no manager and `leaderState` is unconditionally `true`, so there is nothing to
  hand off. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ~L5634, ~L5663.
- **Q:** If no other eligible instance can take over, should the leader still

  `releaseLeadership()` is a stateless file delete with no peer predicate

  **Answer (intake agent):** No additional rate limit beyond the existing
  no-candidate cooldown and election backoff; one step-down per fallback
  dispatch already bounds churn.
- **Q:** Is the fallback a second ranking or a window extension?
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** A bounded window extension of the
  canonical ranking. `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` already re-reads
  `deps.getHerdrListHead` with `current.length + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`
  and returns only the newly visible tail; safety gates remain sequential

# a-r (audit reject) should not change work item priority

## Problem statement

The herdr `a-r` ("audit reject") chord silently overwrites the selected work
item's priority with `medium`. Rejecting an item for rework should reset its
lifecycle state (`open` / `plan_complete`) but must preserve the priority the
producer already assigned, so that a `high` or `critical` item is not
downgraded by the act of rejecting it.

## Users

Producers reviewing `in_review` work items in herdr.

- As a producer, when I press `a-r` to reject an item for rework, I want its
  priority to remain unchanged, so that the triage/urgency signal I set is not
  lost.
- As a producer, when I reject a `critical` item, I want it to stay `critical`
  so it re-enters the queue with the correct urgency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `a-r` (audit reject) shortcut command no longer passes `--priority` to
   `wl update`; a rejected item's priority is left unchanged.
2. The `a-r` shortcut still resets the item's `status` to `open` and `stage`
   to `plan_complete`, and still runs `wl reviewed <id> false` and
   `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` with the rejection summary.
3. The `a-r` shortcut label/description no longer claim a priority reset
   (description reads "reset it to open/plan_complete for rework").
4. Shortcut-config, worklist and herdr shortcut tests are updated to assert the
   priority-preserving behaviour; no test asserts the removed `--priority medium`
   token.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the bundled shortcut definition and its test fixtures.
- Backwards compatibility for `wl update --priority <level>` is unaffected; only
  the `a-r` shortcut stops supplying the flag.
- Keep the `a-y` (audit approve) behaviour unchanged — it already does not
  touch priority.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines the `a-r` chord as:

```text
!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl update <id> --status open --stage plan_complete --priority medium && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no --summary 'Rejected by manual review. <reason>'
```

with description "Reject the in_review item and reset it to
open/plan_complete/medium for rework." This was deliberately introduced by the
now-completed work item WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 ("a-r (audit reject) should reset
item to open/plan_complete/medium"); the priority reset is now considered
undesirable because it destroys the producer's priority signal.

## Desired change

Drop the `--priority medium` token from the `a-r` command chain and update the
shortcut description accordingly, so rejection preserves the item's priority.
Update the affected test fixtures and assertions to match.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Remove `--priority medium` from the `a-r` command; update its `description`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Update the two `a-r` assertions (WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 tests) to expect no `--priority` token.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` compound-command fixture/resolved command.
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` fixture and resolved-command expectation.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Confirm no documented claim of a priority reset; adjust if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2** — "a-r (audit reject) should reset item to open/plan_complete/medium" (completed). Introduced the `--priority medium` token this item removes; direct predecessor.
- **WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9** — rejection reasons with apostrophes no longer break the audit reject shortcut (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV** — audit fingerprint repair affecting the `a-y`/`a-r` background shortcuts (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** — shortcut commands not refreshing the selection list; listed `a-r` among modifying chords (completed).
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — `open_pane: false` background dispatch, used by `a-r`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G** – Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: also, audit, change, chord, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, review, rework, running, sets, shortcut, should, stage, status, when, work
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: also, audit, change, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, review, rework, running, sets, should, stage, status, when, work
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: audit, change, chord, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, running, shortcut, should, stage, status, when, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Intent reversal**: WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 deliberately added the priority reset.
  Assumption: the producer now wants it removed and treats the reset as
  unintended data loss. Documented as a deliberate reversal.
- **Hidden coupling**: other code or docs may assume rejection resets priority.
  Mitigation: repo-wide search for the command string and `plan_complete/medium`
  before/after the change.
- **Test drift**: fixtures copy the command verbatim in several test files;
  mitigation: update all occurrences in one change and let the full suite
  verify.
- **Scope creep**: e.g. adding "restore previous priority" history. Record any
  such idea as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked. The seed context supplied with the
`/intake` invocation was sufficient to draft the brief:

- **Seed**: "When running a-r the command sets the priority of the work item to
  medium. It should not change the priority."
- **Follow-up** — the operator clarified that `a-r` is the herdr
  "audit - reject" chord (a manual producer-audit rejection shortcut) and that
  the priority must not be changed. Source: interactive reply in this session.
- **Research**: located the concrete defect in
  `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (the `a-r` command passes
  `--priority medium`) and its test fixtures. The behaviour was introduced by
  the completed work item WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2; this intake records a deliberate
  reversal of that specific aspect (priority reset), preserving the rest
  (status/stage reset, `reviewed false`, `audit-set`).

# Problem Statement

The HERDR plugin's hydrator task (scheduled every 30s via TaskScheduler) times out approximately every run, causing the UI to become unresponsive for up to 20 seconds. The root cause is that the hydrator spawns multiple `wl`/`herdr` CLI processes sequentially (`wl list --status in-progress`, `herdr pane list`, and `wl dep list` per orphaned item), and these CLI spawns hang or are extremely slow.

# Users

- **HERDR plugin users** (agent operators): The plugin pane becomes unresponsive to keyboard input, commands, and mouse events while the hydrator task is running.
- **AI agent operators**: Agent commands typed during a hydrate timeout are delayed or lost.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified**: The specific CLI call(s) in the hydrator that hang are identified (e.g. `herdr pane list` returning an unbounded number of panes, `wl list --status in-progress` on a large database, etc.).
2. **UI remains responsive during hydrate**: The UI continues to accept and process keyboard input while the hydrator task is running, with no more than 100ms of perceived lag for command input.
3. **Hydrate run bounded**: The hydrator's effective wall-clock time is bounded by its `runTimeoutMs=20s` watchdog, with clear logging of which step timed out.
4. **Child process isolation**: All `execFile` calls used by the hydrator use `{ stdin: 'ignore' }` (or equivalent) to prevent stdin/stdout interference with the TUI.
5. **No regressions**: The full HERDR plugin test suite passes; hydrator tests continue to pass.

# Constraints

- Must not change the hydrator's core behaviour (demoting orphaned in_progress items).
- Must not introduce new dependencies on the TUI event loop.
- The fix should handle workspaces with 50+ panes and 20+ in_progress items without degradation.
- The scheduler's sequential dispatch model should not be changed unless a full redesign is warranted (separate work item).

# Existing State

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`: The hydrator module, 408 lines. Uses `getExecFileAsync()` from `fetcher.ts` for CLI calls.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`: TaskScheduler dispatches tasks sequentially via `await this.runTask()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`: Registers the 'hydrate' task at 30s interval with 20s timeout.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`: `execFileAsync` (promisified `node:child_process.execFile`) — no stdin/stdout isolation.
- The hydrator iterates over every `in_progress` item, and for each without a matching pane, runs `wl dep list` to check for blockers.
- The `runWithTimeout` function resolves on timeout but does not abort the underlying promise; child processes continue running.

# Desired Change

1. Investigate and identify the specific CLI call(s) that hang (add per-step timing/logging).
2. Isolate child process I/O: pass `{ stdin: 'ignore', stderr: 'pipe' }` to all `execFile` calls used by the hydrator.
3. Consider reducing hydrate overhead: limit `herdr pane list` to the current workspace only, cap the number of items processed per tick, or parallelize independent calls.
4. If the scheduler's sequential dispatch is a contributing factor, propose a non-blocking alternative (e.g. fire-and-forget tasks, or at least allow input processing during long-running tasks).

# Key Files (Predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — hydrator orchestration and CLI calls
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `execFileAsync` wrapper (add stdin/stdout isolation)
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `runWithTimeout` and task dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator task registration
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — hydrator tests

# Related Work

- **WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI** — Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane (completed, shipped v1.0.16)
- **WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P** — Worklist: hydrate task + focus-resume (blocked, unimplemented wiring)
- **WL-0MNV0UCPQ003RPIW** — TUI freeze when metadata shows GitHub hint (completed)
- **WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E** — TUI unresponsive to keyboard input (completed, critical)
- **WL-0MSNIX4V60012266** — Compress the space used in herdr plugin meta-data (completed)

# Implement: own-backlog fallback + step-down wiring

parent: WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24

## Goal

Implement the bounded own-backlog dispatch fallback for the coordination-mode
leader and wire the voluntary leadership step-down, satisfying parent AC1–AC9
and turning the test-first children green.

## Implementation sketch

1. **Bounded non-critical tail fetch.** Add a fallback mode to the extended
   tail read in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (extend
   `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` ~L2478 or add a sibling) that re-reads the SAME
   canonical ranking with `current.length + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` and
   returns the newly visible tail **without** the `priority === 'critical'`
   filter. Normal (non-fallback) callers keep the critical-only behaviour.
2. **Fallback selection in the leader path.** In `dispatchFromCoordination`
   (~L3881), only after the coordination entry scan yields no dispatchable
   offer, perform one bounded own-backlog lookup against the leader's OWN
   `opts.cwd` (never another root). Reuse the canonical ranking path
   (`fetchNextItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` via
   `deps.getHerdrListHead`) and the existing sequential safety gates — no
   second ranking, no new ordering.
3. **Report the source.** On a successful own-backlog dispatch, mark the
   outcome machine-readably (e.g. `ownBacklogDispatch: true` on
   `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, ~L2294) so the worker loop can step down.
4. **Step-down wiring.** In the worker loop (near the `dispatchFromCoordination`
   call ~L6303, where `leaderManager` is in scope), call
   `leaderManager.releaseLeadership()` exactly once after the own-backlog
   dispatch completes (claim → marker → spawn already done), set the local
   `leaderState = false`, and do not trigger an immediate self re-election in
   that tick. Legacy mode (`leaderManager === null`) is unchanged.
5. **Fail-open + bounds.** A `{ok:false}`/thrown/empty fallback lookup leaves
   the original terminal reason and never panics; the fallback window stays
   bounded; ownership stays with the leader's own root only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Parent AC1–AC9 are satisfied and the test-first children pass.
2. The fallback runs only when no coordination entry is dispatchable, and only
   against the leader's own `opts.cwd`.
3. Non-critical items beyond the sprint window are eligible only in the
   fallback path; the normal in-view offer path still rejects them.
4. The fallback reuses the canonical ranking with a bounded window and applies
   every existing safety gate as a sequential filter.
5. `releaseLeadership()` is called exactly once after a successful own-backlog
   dispatch, never after a normal in-view dispatch, and never when the
   fallback finds nothing.
6. No new persistence mechanism and no coordination-file schema change.
7. A clean build and the full project test suite pass.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — fallback fetch/selection + outcome flag + loop step-down.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — existing `releaseLeadership()` reused (likely no change).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — deps wiring if a distinct fallback limit is needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts` — tests from the test-first children.
